description: Replace the content-matching submission oracle in src/tmux/dispatch.ts with an unforgeable tmux cursor-geometry oracle, and close the silent-loss gap at the four sendKeysWhenIdle call sites that pass no logEvent.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms display-message -p expands a #{} format string and prints the result rather than showing it in the status line, and that display-message -a lists every format the server knows. CRITICAL HAZARD for this issue: 'an unknown or missing variable is replaced with nothing', so a typo'd or unsupported #{cursor_x} silently expands to an empty field instead of erroring, which would make a naive parser fail OPEN and report every push delivered. The wiki page does not enumerate cursor_x/cursor_y (it defers to the man page, whose FORMATS section truncated on fetch), so the variables were confirmed empirically instead: tmux -L <sock> display-message -p -t 0 '#{cursor_x};#{cursor_y};#{pane_width};#{pane_height}' returned '0;0;80;24' against a real tmux 3.6a server pinned with new-session -x 80 -y 24. The geometry oracle must therefore parse strictly and treat an empty or short field as 'unknown', never as 'delivered'.
officialDocsConsulted.localConventionConflict: tmux's own display-message builder convention is already implemented locally in the vendored src/retry/tmux.ts (buildDisplayArgs), but that builder omits the '-L cam' socket handling that src/tmux/session.ts:tmuxArgs applies and follows an async Bun.spawn convention unreachable from the synchronous dispatch path; the new helper must follow the local tmuxArgs/TmuxSpawnFn convention rather than reusing the vendored builder.

userStories.title: Review round 2 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/tmux/dispatch.ts:462]: The US-R1-001 content backstop indexes the captured pane by cursor_y, but the sidecar's production push path wires a FULL-SCROLLBACK capture reader, so it reads the wrong row. composerLineRetainsPayloadTail (dispatch.ts:304-322) does `capturedContent.split('\n')[cursorY]`, and sendKeysVerified feeds it the injected `capture(paneId)` at dispatch.ts:462. #{cursor_y} is relative to the TOP OF THE VISIBLE PANE, so that indexing is only valid for a visible-screen reader (`capture-pane -p`). src/supervisor/host.ts:579-586 defines capturePane as `capture-pane -p -S - -t <paneId>` (full history), and host.ts:1034-1039 passes exactly that reader into makeNotifyOrchestrator, which forwards it to sendKeysVerified at host.ts:330-336. Reviewer probe on real tmux 3.6a (see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt): with cursor_y=23 on a 24-row pane, `capture-pane -p` line[23] = the true cursor row `bash-3.2$`, while `capture-pane -p -S -` returned 46 lines and line[23] = `SCROLLLINE19`, an arbitrary history line. Consequences on the sidecar path (the highest-traffic push path in the product): (a) the backstop almost always returns false, so the ambiguous geometry branch resolves to `delivered = true` and the exact wrap-boundary residue class the round-1 CRITICAL was raised about stays open there, i.e. the CAM-358 silent loss is NOT closed for the sidecar; (b) conversely, because the sidecar pushes many near-identical `[cam] ...` lines that accumulate in scrollback, a stale history line ending with the payload's 2-to-8 char tail makes the backstop fire on a genuinely delivered push, forcing a resend and tripping the back-to-back send-keys race the PRD calls a hard requirement. This also substantively violates US-002 AC9 ('The verdict is identical whichever capture reader is wired, since the oracle no longer consumes captured content for the delivery decision'): the R1 fix reintroduced captured content into the delivery decision without making it reader-independent, and AC9's mechanical oracle (`! grep -q 'includes(text)'`) cannot detect that. Suggested fix: have sendKeysVerified sample the cursor row itself with a dedicated visible-screen capture (e.g. `capture-pane -p -t <pane>` built in dispatch.ts, or `capture-pane -p -S <cursorY> -E <cursorY>`) instead of reusing the caller-injected capturePaneFn, whose scrollback semantics are unspecified. Same commit should correct the now-false doc comment at test/supervisor/notify-orchestrator.test.ts:280-284, which asserts the verdict 'is no longer derived from capturePaneFn (that reader now only feeds the PRE-send idle-gate)'; that has not been true since dispatch.ts:462 was added. No test covers a scrollback-shaped reader, which is why the suite is green.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/tmux/dispatch.ts:40]: Wrap-boundary axis collision is unhandled under the production Ink composer geometry, so US-002 AC8 ('both directions hold' for an exact-wrap-boundary payload) is not actually demonstrated for production. The module header asserts 'at an exact wrap-boundary payload length the post-send cursor_x can coincidentally equal the baseline cursor_x while cursor_y differs' (dispatch.ts:40-41), and geometryUnchanged (dispatch.ts:247-249) relies on cursor_y to break that tie. But the PRD's own measurement of the real claude TUI records the opposite: 'the Ink composer grows UPWARD from the pane bottom, so a three-row wrapped composer's last row has the SAME cursor_y as an empty composer; measured on a real claude TUI, empty (2,26) vs wrapped (10,26) vs short-filled (33,26)' -- cursor_y is pinned at 26 in all three states, so in production only cursor_x discriminates. A payload whose length lands the composer cursor back on the baseline column therefore yields an identical (x,y) pair for an UNDELIVERED push, which the oracle reports as delivered on attempt 1: exactly the CAM-358 silent-loss defect this issue exists to kill, surviving for one payload-length residue class. The branch's own tests corroborate the contradiction rather than resolving it: the unit constants encode the production y-constant model (test/dispatch.test.ts:344 EMPTY_BASELINE cursorY 26, :347 FILLED_GEOMETRY cursorY 26 -- only x differs), while the integration fixture encodes the inverted y-varying model (test/fixtures/dispatch-geometry/raw-echo.ts:58-61 eager-wraps the cursor DOWN a row on row-fill, so the AC8 boundary test at test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts:169 is discriminated by y, a mechanism that does not exist in the production composer). No test anywhere covers the production collision (baseline x equal AND y equal with text still in the composer). The AC8 integration test consequently passes for a reason that does not hold in production -- the 'fakes lie' class the PRD explicitly warned about ('TEST FIXTURE WARNING ... any threshold calibrated on it is suspect').

userStories.title: Add a shared tmux display-message geometry-query helper
userStories.description: As the dispatch path, I need a synchronous, socket-aware helper that samples a pane's cursor geometry via tmux display-message, so that the submission oracle can key on a shape the payload cannot forge instead of on captured pane text.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/tmux/display-message.ts exports an argv builder and a cursor-geometry sampler that takes a paneId plus a TmuxSpawnFn and returns the sampled geometry. [oracle: file-assert test -f src/tmux/display-message.ts]

The builder routes through tmuxArgs() from src/tmux/session.ts so the '-L cam' socket flag is applied, matching every other dispatch-path tmux call. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'tmuxArgs' src/tmux/display-message.ts]

The multi-field format string uses ';' as the field separator, never a literal TAB (tmux mangles TAB to '_' in format output). [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'cursor_x};#{cursor_y' src/tmux/display-message.ts]

The sampler fails CLOSED on an unusable reading: empty stdout, a non-zero exit, or a field that is not a base-10 integer yields a null/unknown result rather than a fabricated coordinate, because tmux replaces an unknown format variable with nothing instead of erroring. A unit test drives each of those three malformed-output cases and asserts the unknown result. [oracle: bun test test/tmux-display-message.test.ts]

The helper does not import from the vendored src/retry/tmux.ts, whose buildDisplayArgs omits socket handling and uses an async spawn convention. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'retry/tmux' src/tmux/display-message.ts]

A real-tmux integration assertion samples geometry from a pane pinned with new-session -x 80 -y 24 and gets a parseable in-bounds coordinate, gated with test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable). [oracle: bun test test/integration]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: NEW FILE src/tmux/display-message.ts; import tmuxArgs + TmuxSpawnFn from src/tmux/session.ts (tmuxArgs at session.ts:72, SpawnFn at session.ts:81). Model the synchronous spawn shape on defaultCapturePaneFn (src/tmux/dispatch.ts:221-229), which reads r.stdout with the `typeof r.stdout === 'string' ? ... : (r.stdout?.toString() ?? '')` guard. DO NOT reuse src/retry/tmux.ts:16 buildDisplayArgs: it is vendored, omits '-L cam', and its MIT header must stay untouched. Verified against real tmux 3.6a: `display-message -p -t <pane> '#{cursor_x};#{cursor_y};#{pane_width};#{pane_height}'` -> `0;0;80;24`. Fail-closed parsing is load-bearing, not defensive padding: the tmux wiki states an unknown/missing format variable expands to nothing, so a lenient parser would read '' as 0 and report every push delivered (fail-open = the exact silent-loss bug this issue exists to kill). noUncheckedIndexedAccess makes split(';')[n] a `string | undefined`, so the guards are required by the compiler anyway. Real-tmux harness pattern to copy: test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts (dedicated TEST_SOCK, swapSocketSpawn rewriting '-L cam' to the test socket, waitForCondition polling not fixed sleeps, kill-server in beforeEach/afterEach, test.skipIf(!tmuxAvailable)).

userStories.title: Replace the content-matching submission oracle with the geometry oracle
userStories.description: As an operator whose pushed [cam] line must either land exactly once or be retried, I need the submission verdict derived from per-send cursor geometry rather than substring-matching the payload against pane text, so that a wrapped payload is neither silently lost nor sent three times.
acceptanceCriteria: The oracle derives its verdict solely from tmux cursor geometry sampled from the target pane and never substring-matches the payload against captured pane content. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'includes(text)' src/tmux/dispatch.ts]

isComposerEmptied is retired from src/tmux/dispatch.ts and its content-matching unit tests in test/dispatch.test.ts are removed or rewritten against the geometry oracle. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'isComposerEmptied' src/tmux/dispatch.ts]

The empty-composer baseline is sampled per-send from the same pane immediately before send-keys, and the verdict is a comparison of the full (x,y) pair against that baseline; no absolute cursor coordinate is hardcoded anywhere in src/, and the comparison never keys on y alone. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS is retained and the post-send geometry sample still happens after that settle window via the injected sleepFn. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS' src/tmux/dispatch.ts]
When the geometry sample is unknown (US-001 fail-closed result), the payload is treated as NOT delivered and retried, never as delivered. [oracle: bun test test/dispatch.test.ts]

A real-tmux integration test at a pane pinned to new-session -x 80 drives an UNDELIVERED wrapping payload end to end and asserts send-keys is attempted maxAttempts times and exactly one push-undelivered event is emitted. [oracle: bun test test/integration]
That same real-tmux test drives a payload that IS successfully submitted and asserts exactly ONE send-keys call and ZERO push-undelivered events. [oracle: bun test test/integration]

That same real-tmux test includes a payload sized to land exactly on the wrap boundary for the pinned pane width, not merely an arbitrarily long one, and both directions hold for it. [oracle: bun test test/integration]

The verdict is identical whichever capture reader is wired, since the oracle no longer consumes captured content for the delivery decision. [oracle: file-assert ! grep -q 'includes(text)' src/tmux/dispatch.ts]
sendKeysVerified still returns void; its signature is unchanged. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'export function sendKeysVerified(opts: SendKeysVerifiedOptions): void' src/tmux/dispatch.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Edit src/tmux/dispatch.ts (isComposerEmptied at :211-216, sendKeysVerified loop at :291-353, SEND_KEYS_SETTLE_MS at :132); update test/dispatch.test.ts (isComposerEmptied describe at :320-330, exported import at :36); NEW test/integration/dispatch-geometry.test.ts. THE LIVE DEFECT: isComposerEmptied evaluates lines.slice(-5).some(l => l.includes(text)); a wrapped payload never appears whole on any single line, so it ALWAYS reports delivered, breaks the retry loop on attempt 1, and emits no event. WHY GEOMETRY: cursor position is unforgeable by payload text (a '>' or '->' at column 0 of a soft-wrap boundary forges the old regex anchor, and '->' is realistic in [cam] status text) and is independent of which of the three production capture readers is wired (src/supervisor/host.ts:579 full scrollback, host.ts:270 visible screen, dispatch.ts:221 visible screen default). GOTCHA cursor_y alone is useless: the Ink composer grows UPWARD from the pane bottom, so a three-row wrapped composer's last row has the SAME cursor_y as an empty composer; measured on a real claude TUI, empty (2,26) vs wrapped (10,26) vs short-filled (33,26). cursor_x carries the discriminating signal: compare the PAIR. GOTCHA never hardcode a coordinate: /help relocated the cursor to (9,6) in the same pane whose empty baseline is (2,26), so only a per-send baseline comparison is sound. GOTCHA settle stays load-bearing: after a genuine submit the cursor reads the empty baseline at t+0, which is ALSO what an un-rendered pane reads before typed text appears, so geometry does not remove the settle requirement. GOTCHA exact-wrap-boundary collision: when the payload lands exactly on a wrap boundary the cursor can rest at the continuation row's start column, which may EQUAL the baseline x, which is why the wrap-boundary-sized payload is a required test case and not a nice-to-have. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE HARD REQUIREMENTS: a delivered payload resent trips the back-to-back send-keys race (scripts/cam/patterns.md:330, 'the orchestrator Ink prompt does not absorb back-to-back send-keys calls'), and an undelivered payload reported delivered is the original CAM-358 silent loss. TEST FIXTURE WARNING: test/integration/sendkeys-submit.test.ts uses `cat`, which DOUBLE-echoes (kernel tty echo + cat echo-back) and does not model the production Ink TUI in raw mode; any threshold calibrated on it is suspect. Geometry is testable with a plain tty receiver precisely because it does not depend on the receiver's echo/render behaviour, but to drive the UNDELIVERED direction you need a receiver that swallows the trailing Enter (a small raw-stdin fixture script that echoes typed chars and ignores \r), since `cat` always submits. Argv-shape tests with scripted capturePaneFn stubs structurally CANNOT catch this class of defect (they return exactly the string the code expects) - every regression in this issue's history was found by real-tmux probes, so the new coverage must drive a real tmux server. DO NOT resume, branch from, or cherry-pick the parked branch cam/abandoned/issue-358-oracle-attempt (origin 64e2a909): it holds the abandoned content-matching attempt and is reference material only. Reuse the US-001 helper; do not re-implement the format query inline.

userStories.title: Thread logEvent into the four sendKeysWhenIdle call sites
userStories.description: As an operator debugging a push that never landed, I need every production push path to emit push-undelivered on retry exhaustion, so that a lost line leaves a trace in the event log instead of vanishing silently.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/issue.ts passes a logEvent into its sendKeysWhenIdle call. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'logEvent' src/commands/issue.ts]
src/commands/review.ts passes a logEvent into its sendKeysWhenIdle call. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'logEvent' src/commands/review.ts]

The production default sink for each call site is the file event logger writing .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl, adapted to the bare (kind, detail) seam sendKeysVerified expects. [oracle: file-assert grep -q 'adaptLogEventForPush' src/commands/issue.ts]
Each call site accepts an injectable logEvent override so tests can wire makeInMemoryEventLogger instead of touching the real event log. [oracle: bun test]

A test drives retry exhaustion through at least one of the four command paths and asserts exactly one push-undelivered event reaches the injected sink, rather than asserting only that a mock was called. [oracle: bun test]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

userStories.notes: Call sites: src/commands/issue.ts:185, src/commands/review.ts:183, src/commands/spec.ts:218, src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts:417 (inside makeSignalPaneFn). REUSE, do not rebuild: adaptLogEventForPush is already exported at src/supervisor/host.ts:285 and converts a WorkerEventLogger into the bare `(kind, detail) => void` seam sendKeysVerified's logEvent expects (see host.ts:289 for the ts/storyId/uuid wrapping, which uses uuid 'sidecar'; pick an equivalent per-command uuid rather than copying 'sidecar' blindly). makeFileEventLogger is at src/supervisor/events.ts:668; the established default-sink idiom is `options.logEvent ?? makeFileEventLogger(join(cwd, '.claude', 'cam-worker-events.jsonl'))`, already used at src/commands/journal.ts:618 and src/commands/issue-specify.ts:276 - follow it rather than inventing a new one. issue.ts/review.ts/spec.ts already thread optional capturePaneFn/sleepFn/idleTimeoutMs through their options objects, so logEvent is an additive optional field in the same shape. orch-recycle-watch.ts differs: makeSignalPaneFn closes over tmuxSpawnFn only, so the logEvent has to be threaded into that factory. makeInMemoryEventLogger (events.ts:679) returns { logger, events } for assertions. Per the test-quality invariant, assert on the captured event payload, not on the fact that a mock was called.

MIN_PAYLOAD_TAIL_MATCH = 2 is a loose anchor: a 2-char endsWith match is cheap to hit by coincidence, and a false positive here costs a duplicate push (the back-to-back send-keys race). The 2-char floor is only needed for the exact residue where the composer's trailing row holds precisely the prompt-width remnant; consider deriving the expected remnant length from the sampled paneWidth and cursorX (both already in CursorGeometry) instead of scanning a range of suffix lengths, which would make the check exact rather than probabilistic.

Carried over unresolved from review round 1: the idleTimeoutMs JSDoc still reads 'Default: 5 000' in all three thin-proxy commands (issue.ts:83, review.ts:82, spec.ts:117), but the effective default has been IDLE_WAIT_DEADLINE_MS = 30_000 since CAM-358 (dispatch.ts:200, consumed at dispatch.ts:414). Pre-existing drift the diff correctly did not touch under surgical-changes discipline.

src/tmux/dispatch.ts was raised 365 -> 534 (+46%) across this branch, with a well-argued _ref staged in the same commit, so the raise is justified rather than papering over a split. Noting for the next story in this file: dispatch.ts now carries three distinct concerns (idle detection, the geometry delivery oracle plus its content backstop, and the logEvent adapters at :511-533). If it grows again, the logEvent adapter pair is the natural extraction.
